name: Shielding
description: A strong charge next to the beam line throws the beam out of the arena. A grounded metal plate between them screens its field: the charge it induces on the plate cancels much of the field on the far side. Place a grounded plate.

reality.represents: Electrostatic shielding by a grounded plate

remarks.detail: The charge the field induces on the grounded plate cancels much of it beyond the plate.
A plate screens only partly: the field reaches round its edges. A closed grounded box (a Faraday cage) would screen completely.

remarks.line: Real plates and their fringe fields
remarks.detail: The electrodes are metal boxes standing on the plane, their surface charge solved exactly (boundary elements): uniform between plates, bulging out past their ends, and rearranging when charges come near, as in a real instrument.

Everything is symmetric about the plane z = 0, so the particle never leaves it. A real beam also has a width across the plane, where the same fields act differently (focusing in the plane can defocus across it).
